evidence:
Source-review Pass for the row-34 verification procedure, with only partial runtime corroboration. Inspected the actual frozen rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx using openpyxl: Quality Checks!A35:E35 is check 34 and says judges must click, wait, resize or toggle rather than score first paint; Internal Quality Checks!A35:Z35 repeats the requirement with no additional annotation. The frozen Harbor references/quality-checks.md section 34 operationalizes this as whether the judge is told to perform those actions. The references/staged-task-contract.md sections judge.toml and prompt.md/app_context.md and deterministic-checks.md check-rubric-prompt.py require browser tools, rendered evidence and prompt injection of criteria. All five task judge files provide Playwright and all prompts inject their criteria. Public instruction.md paragraph 4 and environment/instructions/ui.md require keyboard use, a narrow screen and both themes; behaviour.md requires five-second execution budgets, delayed preview interaction and debounced Auto-run.

The complete set of functional descriptors maps to executed protocols, not static inspection. In .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-postrepair-audit/task/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:13 the judge must record actual elapsed times; :15 says to batch timed actions and confirm pending state. S02 at :134 and :137 requires actual pre-/post-CSS button clicks; :149 requires a working four-second timer then observation until at least five seconds after its replacement. S03 at :158 says to leave the completed preview untouched for at least six seconds and click; :159 repeats a six-second idle before actual key/input events. S04 at :178-180 requires cancellation before a genuinely pending callback, then waiting beyond its due time. S09 :249-259 requires observing loop termination and recovery. S12 :300 and S13 :323 explicitly wait for asynchronous errors. S15 requires expanding actual console values. S17 requires measured automatic execution, repeated real edits inside the observed debounce interval, and full measured-delay-plus-margin observation after switching off. S21-S24 require real saves, loads, reloads, two live dirty editors, and completed process restart. S34 requires two actual theme changes affecting chrome, editor and console while comparing recorded working state. S36 requires a ten-second batched observation of nested callbacks. These instructions cannot legitimately be completed from the initial rendered frame.

The remaining dimensions also exercise their applicable changes. tests/gates/render/judge.toml:25 requires an authored marker and pressing Run; gates/constraints/judge.toml:25-27 requires UI Save and independent-context load/reload. tests/scored/polish/prompt.md:45 and :47 require actual keyboard events, operating an example picker, loading a saved snippet and observing focus. Its judge.toml:23 requires that editor, preview and console can each be reached and used at roughly 390 by 844; :68 requires activation and visible feedback. tests/scored/visual/prompt.md:35-37 requires desktop and mobile surfaces plus both offered themes, and visual/judge.toml:99 requires comparison of the same surfaces at both sizes. All task paths in this paragraph are under the frozen task directory above.

Raw evidence was checked directly, without consulting reviewer reports. RESULTS.json SHA256 equals the raw-evidence-index binding ec88c00c12336257196e209f427a40690b76b4d3fc7f283656bc67735cf1bc09. All 23 listed app-file hashes match the frozen app; functional judge/prompt hashes match, as do the inspected runtime_flow.cjs, workspace_flow.cjs and surface_flow.cjs driver hashes. RESULTS.json post.facts.S03.later_interactions records click/key/input counts 1/1/1 after 6104.75 ms and 6103.31 ms idle periods. runtime_flow.cjs:38-45 actually waits 6100 ms and invokes click/press actions. workspace_flow.cjs:161-201 enters real source, measures debounce, repeatedly edits, and waits the derived off-state interval; the raw first automatic delay was 559.05 ms. workspace_flow.cjs:296-305 clicks theme twice and compares rendered styles/work; pre.facts.S34.theme_work_preserved records identical draft/preview/console state and actual chrome/editor/console style changes. surface_flow.cjs:32-35 clicks theme, calls setViewportSize({width:390,height:844}), performs an authored mobile Run and clears the console; surface-results.json records that mobile action/readback. These are direct scripted browser observations, not configured judge scores. The raw evidence explicitly says criterion_verdicts_produced=false and full_current_criterion_run_claimed=false; the index reports no full configured verifier, Oracle, target-model or measured judge workload. Thus this Pass establishes action-bearing grading instructions, not a claim that the configured LLM judge completed every action or passed the task.

Counterexample analysis: a visually convincing preview with handlers removed after five seconds would fail S03's delayed click and focused-input evidence even if its first paint looked correct; a toggle changing only its label would fail S34's actual appearance checks; a desktop-only layout hiding mobile panes cannot satisfy the mobile reach/use observation. No credible still-first-paint false pass was found. A conforming alternative with tabbed mobile panes, a drawer library, native focus outlines, light-first theming, and a static restored preview after Stop is explicitly allowed in the prompts and criteria, so those implementation choices do not create a false failure for this row.
